title: The Sky Here
summary: Three suns, two moons and a night aurora

blocks.text: Hoanna's sky is much darker than the Overworld's: at noon the zenith is a dim slate violet, turning warmer and yellower towards the horizon — that is the dust hanging in the air. The ground is lit just as brightly as at home; only the sky is dark.

There are three suns: the main one and two faint remnant suns that rise and set with it. At night there are two moons: the large one shows the same phase as the Overworld's moon, the small companion is always half a cycle apart.

The night sky is full of faint violet stars, and an <t>MRU</t> aurora stretches across it — bluish near the horizon, fading into magenta higher up — slowly turning with the stars. Now and then a silent arc flickers over the distant horizon; the next one comes at least a dozen seconds later.

items: Day, night and weather follow the Overworld: when the sun rises there, it rises here; when it rains there, it rains over the corrupted lands and the Hoanna Sea (not over the Dreadlands or the desert).
If the arcs bother you, turn on the vanilla accessibility option "Hide Lightning Flashes": they get much dimmer and half as frequent.

blocks.text: The original research book first sells Hoanna as "the land of dreams", "the world of limitless possibilities" — and only on the radiation page admits that it is really a nuclear wasteland. What happened there, nobody knows.
